The bird known for its ability to repeat what you say is the parrot.

In this alternative ending, Margo corners The Phantom not in the Louvre, but in a secluded aviary in the countryside. The thief, desperate to escape, attempts to bluff his way out by mimicking Margo’s voice using a sophisticated recording device, trying to confuse her guards. However, Margo, noticing a real parrot in the cage beside him, realizes the thief is relying on auditory deception. She calmly asks the parrot to repeat what the thief just said. The bird, having heard the thief’s true confession moments before, squawks the incriminating words clearly. Margo arrests him, and while the brotherly connection is never revealed, the case is closed with the help of the very bird known for repeating what it hears.
